title: Tokyo's Odia Diaspora Keeps Chandan Yatra Alive Across Oceans
excerpt: The Odisha Community Japan marks Lord Jagannath's 42-day Sandalwood Festival, carrying a Puri tradition 5,000 miles east.
body:
Odia families in Tokyo gathered this spring to observe Chandan Yatra, the sacred 42-day Sandalwood Festival dedicated to Lord Jagannath — bringing a ritual rooted in Puri's ancient temple complex into the heart of Japan.

**What the festival marks:**
Chandan Yatra, which began on Akshaya Tritiya (April 30, 2025) and runs through June 11, is the longest festival observed at the Jagannatha Temple in Puri, India. For 21 of those days, representative idols of the deities are carried in procession to the Narendra Tirtha tank and given ceremonial boat rides, while priests apply fragrant sandalwood paste to provide cooling relief during summer. The festival also signals the formal start of chariot construction for the world-famous Ratha Yatra.

**Why Tokyo matters:**
The Odisha Community Japan Tokyo (OCJT), a registered non-profit cultural organization in Koto-ku, Tokyo, has maintained a calendar of Jagannath-centered celebrations in Japan since 2005. A sister body, NPO Odisha Community Japan (OCJ), celebrated its 18th consecutive Rath Yatra in Kawasaki in June 2025. The Indian Embassy Tokyo has formally recognized the role these groups play in deepening India-Japan cultural ties, noting that 'such celebrations give an opportunity to the younger generation to carry forward Indian traditions.' Japanese locals have joined the festivities alongside Odia participants, turning a regional Odia ritual into an act of cross-cultural exchange.

**What to watch:**
With Ratha Yatra 2025 confirmed for June 27 in Kawasaki, the diaspora's festival season is far from over — and pressure to expand Chandan Yatra observances to other Japanese cities is quietly growing.
